scope: public literature, no lower date cutoff; bounded first 8 web / 12 paper / 15 related results; no exhaustive claim

claims.F1: The selected-gene model can inform a drug experiment; challenge allele, phase, residual-function and tissue transfer assumptions.
claims.F2: mTOR inhibition might improve a qualified deficit; reject directional inference if activation is compensatory or fidelity/function worsens.
claims.F3: BUBR1 abundance changes might be useful; reject rescue inference without localization, checkpoint and tissue function.
claims.F4: An apparent response is functional benefit; reject if explained by arrest, cell loss, survivor selection or lost later output.
claims.F5: A usable exposure window might exist; reject unsupported nominal-culture to clinical-exposure bridging.
claims.F6: Non-cancer safety might be adequate; challenge developmental, muscle, renal, immune and interaction assumptions.
claims.F7: Tumour evidence might support a separate direction; challenge subtype/backbone and normal-tissue selectivity transfer.
claims.F8: No better-supported alternative is currently prioritized; seek genuine functional counterexamples and failed rescue routes.
